top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) are a mature, independently reproduced capability: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift by design and has reached the 1e-18 level, and the same instruments now give millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on variation of constants and dark matter searches. That is physics clues from nature and not elegant theory alone, it is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and a two-name allocation is clean. Moire graphene (P002) is a strong second, but I prefer to keep it and the three-name allocation including Bistritzer for later; an award is better than no award.
